parts.text: Nancy is returning her overdue books to the library.
She owes $0.50 cents each on 8 books.
However, the library has a policy that if more than half of the books returned are overdue, an additional $1.00 fee per book is added.
Plus, there is a flat $2.00 fee for having at least one book that's over a week overdue.
If 5 out of the 8 books are overdue, how much does she have to pay in total?

parts.text: Rita hand-picks Junebugs off of her plants every summer.
On Monday, she removed 390 Junebugs.
On both Tuesday and Wednesday, she removed twice as many Junebugs as she did on Monday.
Thursday she removed 480 and on Friday she removed 570.
What is the average number of Junebugs that she removes per day?

parts.text: Joe has twice as many cars as Robert, who has 20 cars.
Joe decides to sell 20% of his cars during a summer sale.
After the sale, he gives away twice as many cars as the number he sold to his mother, who then donates half of them to a charity.
If the charity's donation does not affect Joe's total number of cars, how many cars does Joe remain with after selling some and giving some to his mother?

parts.text: In a set of magicians cards, there are 1500 red cards, and 60% more green cards.
Yellow cards are as many as the sum of red and green cards.
How many cards of all mentioned colors are there?

parts.text: Conor lives near a beach and loves going there every day to have fun.
On a particular week, he found 5000 people at the beach on the first day.
The following day, 2000 more people were present at the beach than on the first day, and on the third day, the total number of people increased to twice the number that were there on the second day.
If Conor saw an average of 6000 people each day for the rest of the week, calculate the total number of people Conor saw at the beach that week.
